schema.op: memory_write | memory_delete | episode_record | task (host-only action that is not a pure edit)
schema.args: the stigmergy call arguments VERBATIM (memory_write: key/description/content; episode_record: its fields incl. memory_keys) so the host session replays op(args) with no interpretation; for task: {instruction}
schema.why: evidence per CLAUDE.md's Evidence Policy — commit hashes, gate runs, measurements
schema.requested: {date, branch, commit} of the work that made the edit necessary

protocol: Producers (sessions without stigmergy tools) APPEND one line per needed edit, in the same commit as the work that makes it necessary. The consumer (a host session with stigmergy) applies each entry and DELETES its line in the SAME commit that applies it — lifting anything durable into a properly-keyed memory first. Applied entries are never kept or struck through; this file shrinks back toward this README line (the handoff-purge rule). Parsers skip op == 'README'. This line is permanent.

args.description: Link cable Stage 2 COMPLETE 2026-08-22: UART transport live end-to-end, two-instance linkcheck green, cable_club_nolink golden landed; IPX/TCP remain Stage 5 (planned, unstarted).
args.content: The message-level HAL seam works end-to-end over the UART transport: pret serial primitives unchanged above the line; below it net_hal session core (HELLO/token election -> GB-establishment synthesis: master 'receives' $02/USING_INTERNAL_CLOCK, slave $01), net_frame codec/ARQ (SOF $A5, CRC16-CCITT, stop-and-wait, seq 1..255; timers denominated in WALL FRAMES of the 60 Hz PIT tick_count via the nf_clock pointer since 3222bbd — they were pump-call-denominated before, which collapsed the 10 s death timeout to ~1 s wall and was the whole 2026-08-22 'stall'; the DOSBox-X nullmodem was exonerated), and com_uart byte driver (8250/16550, IRQ RX ring + post-IER drain + CLI-guarded polled fallback; master kicks held while net_estab_pend to keep the first kick from overtaking the queued ESTABLISH_REQ). Proven by tools/linkcheck.sh (two DOSBox-X instances over nullmodem, C_MODEM fork binary required): 3/3 consecutive green — $02/$01 role split, LINKLOG cross-check both directions (~662 records), zero desyncs, both sides parked in LinkMenu and NS_ESTABLISHED at the synchronized photograph (LINKCHECK_MENU_HOLD frames after linkcheck_in_menu). Single-player regression: fidelity-serial 16/16 and fidelity-full-serial 90/90 PASS 2026-08-22. The receptionist no-peer path has a golden: cable_club_nolink (id 91, tier full). Transport debugging aid: the fork's mcp-debug branch (Happyarch/dosbox-x, 0eff618fd, submodule pointer tracks it) carries an NMDBG 1 Hz nullmodem heartbeat (rx_state/gather-buffer/byte counters) — use it for Stage 3 block transfers and the future IPX/TCP transports. IPX and TCP transports are Stage 5 of docs/current_plan_link_cable.md: planned, unstarted; slirp reachability spike gates the NE2000 path.

args.description: DURABLE architecture decision 2026-08-23 (99cb00b): the whole cable-club session (and the trade.asm cinematic, and Stage 4's pre-battle screens) runs inside the movie-projection surface, NOT a bespoke UI layout.
args.content: CableClub_DoBattleOrTrade arms MovieBeginSurface (160x144 GB surface centred on the 320x200 canvas, per-frame stride-40->stride-32 mirror via g_surface_redraw_cb, GB OBJ-over-window z-order); teardown at MovieEndSurface before predef InitOpponent (battle owns its canvas), in ReturnToCableClubRoom before LoadMapData, and on the index-$ff DisplayTitleScreen path; re-arm after StatusScreen returns in TradeCenter_DisplayStats. Every pret hlcoord/bccoord X,Y becomes CC(X,Y) = wTileMap + ((Y)+UI_TITLE_ROW)*SCREEN_WIDTH + ((X)+UI_TITLE_COL) (UI_TITLE_COL=10, UI_TITLE_ROW=3 - numerically identical to battle BCOORD, so PrintWaitingText serves trade and battle unchanged). Menus: pret set/res BIT_DOUBLE_SPACED_MENU kept faithfully AND realized by menu_item_step = 2*SCREEN_WIDTH vs SCREEN_WIDTH around each HandleMenuInput. faithdiff note: the CC macro name is captured by PORT_STORE_RE as if it were a store target - suppressed tree-wide via tools/faithdiff_suppress.json stores entry 'CC' (justified there). Scanner-attribution trap re-confirmed: a body attributes to the label IMMEDIATELY preceding it, so a pret label must precede its port-only alias (WaitForAPress/WaitForTextScrollButtonPress order in src/home/joypad2.asm).

args.description: OPEN presentation gap 2026-08-23 (da6f486): trade.asm's cable-continuation scroll effect (GB_TILEMAP1 second BG plane) is not composited by the single-surface cinematic model - memory writes faithful, visual effect absent. Retiring it = extending ppu.asm's window model (maintainer call).
args.content: pret's Trade_AnimLeftToRight/RightToLeft use a two-plane trick: the cable row is seeded into vBGMap1 ($9C00) via Trade_CopyCableTilesOffScreen + RedrawRowOrColumn while the main scene scrolls on vBGMap0, so the cable visually continues off-screen. The port's movie-projection surface composites ONE window sourcing GB_TILEMAP0 only; the port translation writes GB_TILEMAP1 faithfully (byte-for-byte, RedrawRowOrColumn machinery live) but nothing draws that plane in this configuration, so the specific cable-continuation frames render without the second plane's contribution. pret's own comment calls the FIRST call site pointless (blank tiles onto blank tiles) - only the two mid-animation sites lose visuals. Not a data/logic divergence: the trade itself, all WRAM/OAM state, and every other frame of the cinematic are unaffected. Fix would extend src/ppu/ppu.asm's window descriptor model to a second BG source; that is a maintainer decision. Flagged by the step-3 implementer review, recorded at docs/current_plan_link_cable.md Stage 3.

args.title: Link cable Stage 3: Trade Center code-complete in one session (block seam, cable_club, trade.asm, harnesses, golden) under a mid-session deferred-dynamics directive
args.narrative: Remote session (no stigmergy), branch claude/link-cable-protocol-planning-s5d09u, continuing the Stage 2 close-out session. Workflow per maintainer directive: Haiku collects facts, Sonnet implements against a ROOT-written spec in an isolated worktree, ROOT reviews the diff adversarially and re-runs every check before commit. Steps: (1) NF_BLK block seam + Serial_ExchangeBytes re-cut, verified by NETTEST layout v2 (one-shot drop ARQ proof at 424 B - periodic faults can never let a large frame through) and linkcheck regression (b50e1e0). (2) cable_club.asm completed to all 23 labels on the movie-projection surface with CC(X,Y)=+10/+3; entry path live via bills_pc hidden events + the restored CableClub_Run poll in WaitForTextScrollButtonPress; fidelity-serial core 16/16 (99cb00b). ROOT review then found two real gaps the plan had flagged: the trade path never reached the .dsv disk seam (fixed 4f75640) and the serial death-hatch $FF flowed onward as data (fixed 5eeb434: cable_club_link_down through pret's own index-$ff title reset; without it - enemy-mon index $FF ~10KB past the tilemap, a one-sided trade past the dec-al confirm, unbounded preamble-hunt scans). (3) trade.asm+trade2.asm all 53 labels (da6f486); implementer verified RGBDS precedence of ICON_TRADEBUBBLE<<2+n against the compiled ROM (0x38-0x3B) and flagged the GB_TILEMAP1 two-plane gap honestly. (4-6) tradecheck harness + --kill + in_game_trade golden (da5f81a, 9bb5fe6): the received mon lands at the LAST party slot (remove_mon shift-up + add_mon append), so 'sent' only exists in a pre-walk GBSEED.BIN dump; --kill asserts the sticky link_down_hatch mark because a post-reset NEW GAME init can rewrite wTradeCenterPointerTableIndex. MID-SESSION DIRECTIVE (maintainer): defer ALL dynamic checks until the whole plan closes (serial VM bottleneck), keep committing+pushing - so steps 3-6 carry static-tier verification only and the plan doc gained an explicit END-OF-PLAN DYNAMIC BATTERY item. Infrastructure incident: /dev/null was found clobbered into a regular file (zsh shell-snapshot stderr had been written into it), which broke git commit via the prepare-commit-msg hook's `git hash-object -t tree /dev/null` ('too-short tree object'); restored with os.mknod. Dead end preserved: none of the three worktree agents could run make image until CWSDPMI.EXE (deliberately uncommitted) was copied from .toolchain/ - expect this in every fresh worktree.
